findings.title: Relocate docs leave out the new refusal while a move runs
findings.body: This push moves `busy: busyNow` into `activeTransactionDeps()` (`main/workspaces/index.ts:347`). As a result, `relocateRefusal` (`relocate.ts:24`) now also refuses "Change folder…" with `moving` while a group move runs, and `relocate-copy.ts:35` shows `relocateMoving` for it. The `workspaces:relocate` row here still says it is refused only "while a recording or export runs". The backlog banner says the same (`backlog/several-workspaces.md:26`). Consider adding "or a move" in both places.

thread_replies.reply: Confirmed. The catch at index.ts:215-217 now calls `refusalOfError`, and move-group.ts:62-66 maps `StaleWorkspaceError` to stale, `MaintenanceError` to maintenance and anything else to io.
Confirmed. The `.catch` at index.ts:174-177 clears `deviceId` before it rethrows, so the next group retries the read.
Confirmed. The `skipped` doc (workspaces.ts:253-254) now says only Stop fills it, and that a group refused as a whole lists every item in `failed`. This matches `refuseAll`.
Confirmed. No `move.*` string in es.json uses "workspace" as the term any more. The only remaining match is the "Default workspace" name in `locationParentMissing`.

structuredOutput.summary: I found no bugs in this push. The `moving` lock now applies to relocate as well as to switch: `busy` moved into `activeTransactionDeps`, so `relocateRefusal` and the switch transaction both see `busyNow`. The relocate refusal type, its message mapping and the en/es strings cover the new reason. The other new strings (`relocateNotWorkspace`, `relocateFailed`) are wired up and tested, and the spec's IPC table is now a single merged table. One consider: the spec row for `workspaces:relocate` and the backlog banner still say \"Change folder…\" is refused only while a recording or export runs; they don't mention a move. The 4 earlier threads on these files are all addressed. The spec still lists a `workspaces:move-item` row; it was kept on purpose and marks that row as not a channel of its own.
